builds.howItPlays: You kill your own cheap units that pay you back when they die (a card, a rune or Gold) with spells like Deathgrip and Cull the Weak, and Karthus, Eternal makes each of those death effects happen twice. Whenever you conquer or hold a battlefield, LeBlanc can make a temporary copy of a unit there, and a copied Ruined Rex, which deals 4 damage to an enemy unit when it dies, keeps your opponent's side thin until your biggest units finish the game.
builds.whyYou: You like a plan with a lot of small decisions: which of your own units to kill, when to do it, and which one LeBlanc should copy. Losing a unit doesn't bother you when it draws a card or takes an enemy down with it, and you'd rather build a steady lead than race. If working out the right order for your plays sounds more fun than attacking every turn, LeBlanc fits you well.
builds.ratingNotes: Re-rated 2026-09-25 from the deck picks. Coordinates moved from 4.5/6/6.5/7 to 5/5/7.5/4. Variance dropped most: the old rating read guide quotes about lopsided games, while the scored lists run mostly 3-ofs, have no reveal or luck cards and draw a lot of cards. The old deckListUrl was the bare /decks page. Scored decks (pace/stance/complexity/variance): LeBlanc - No Hook Set 4 (Alex Contri) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/d11f96ce-f2c0-49fa-9c2d-f2c57fcc9dc6 4.5/5/7.5/4.5 Midrange; LeBlanc Hookless (beef) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/ac2afee1-695d-4b2d-8a33-08000373bcf3 5/5/7.5/4 Midrange; Deathknell Leblanc (rexosorous) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/4dcc25d1-323f-4659-bad0-6ff91bc35274 5/5/7.5/3.5 Midrange. Mean (tools.ts style): Midrange 5/5/7.5/4, labels Midrange x3. Adjustments on every sheet: stance +0.5 (the Legend puts extra ready units on battlefields you already contest); complexity +1 (the Legend asks on each conquer or hold whether to discard for a Reflection and which unit to copy; Dusk Rose Lab adds a sacrifice decision each Beginning Phase). What decided each Axis: Pace, 8-9 cheap Deathknell units (Soaring Scout, Watchful Sentry, Honest Broker) against 10-11 cards costing 5+ (Glasc Mixologist, Ruined Rex, Thousand-Tailed Watcher, Rift Herald). Stance, few pressure cards (about 3), about 7-8 answers (Hidden Blade, Cull the Weak, Deathgrip) and a large own-plan share, so balance is slightly negative and lands at 5. Complexity, 24-27 setup cards (Deathknell, Mighty for Sacrifice, Mirror Image), 10-11 reactive cards and the Legend's copy choice. Variance, no luck or swing cards, 6-7 removal and 8-12 card-flow cards; Alex Contri's list has fewer 3-ofs (0.38) and sits higher at 4.5. No Axis had a formula-versus-judgment gap of 2 or more. Legend ability: when you conquer or hold, you may discard 1 and exhaust LeBlanc to play a ready Reflection token there that becomes a copy of another unit there, with Temporary.
